title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 43
paragraphs: When Adrastus had answered Croesus with words like these, they afterward set out, provided with chosen young men and with dogs. When they had come to Mount Olympus, they tracked the beast, and having found it and taken their stand in a circle around it, they began hurling their spears at it. Then the guest—the one who had been purified of manslaughter, whose name was Adrastus—hurling a spear at the boar, missed it and struck the son of Croesus instead. So, being struck by the spear-point, the young man fulfilled the saying of the dream. Someone ran to report what had happened to Croesus, and having come to Sardis, he made known to him the combat and the fate of his son. Croesus was overwhelmed with grief at the death of his son, and he was moved all the more to lamentation by this fact: that his son had been slain by the very man whom he himself had purified of manslaughter. Grievously troubled by the misfortune, he called upon Zeus the Purifier, protesting to him what he had suffered at his guest’s hands, and he called moreover upon the Protector of Suppliants and the Guardian of Friendship—naming the same god each time—calling upon him as Protector of Suppliants because, when he had received the guest into his house, he had been unknowingly nourishing the slayer of his son, and as Guardian of Friendship because, having sent him as a protector, he had found him to be the worst of foes.”
